messages:
aisha: Heads-up — saw a ~22% p50 latency regression on the llama-13b path when we enabled the new dynamic-shape specialization in the compile pass. Repro: canary with varying seq lengths (8/64/256 interleaved).

ben: Ugh. Did the kernel selector flip to a different GEMM kernel or to a non-cuGraph capture path? Any profiler output?

aisha: Quick dump from the perf trace attached to the canary:
```
NVTX: forward: aten::matmul kernel=gemm_sm80_tf32 (chosen_by=autotuner_v2)
NVTX: cudagraph capture: skipped (shape_variance>threshold)
timeline: kv-cache copy spikes during 256 runs
avg token time: baseline 12.6ms -> canary 15.4ms
autotuner: decision log -> pick_id=17 (specialized) for len<=64, else pick_id=4 (generic)
```

aisha: The weird bit is that torch.compile seems to fold shape guards that end up preventing the old cudagraph capture entrypoint. So the runtime falls back to continuous-batching path which has worse latency at small batches.

kai: Can you paste the exact compile flags? I remember we toggled shape_specialization=True and specialize_on_batch=False last week.

maria: Also tagging infra-bot for GPU telemetry: @infra-bot can you pull the SM utilization + active_warps for those runs?

infra-bot: Collected. Summary:
- 256 seq: avg SM util 92%, active_warps 31
- 64 seq: avg SM util 78%, active_warps 19
- 8 seq: avg SM util 44%, active_warps 8
Note: cudagraph-enabled runs show lower kernel launch overhead (0.5ms) vs fallback (1.3ms).

ben: Looks like two interacting effects: (1) shape-specialized kernels cause different entrypoints that our cudagraph capture heuristic doesn't consider compatible; (2) autotuner picks specialized kernels that are better for steady-state but worse when capture is disabled.

kai: Quick experiment idea: prefer generic kernel when capture_compatible flag==false and batch variance > X. That would avoid the bad combo. We should also log the capture_compatibility per kernel in the autotuner traces.

aisha: Agreed. I ran a small patch locally where the kernel score included a +15% penalty if capture_compatible==false AND seq_variance>0.5. Result: p50 back to 12.9ms, tail unchanged. But throughput for long-256 steady runs drops ~3%.

maria: That tradeoff is acceptable for our PLG use-case where p50 is more visible. We should gate it behind a rollout flag and add a metric in console for "capture-compatibility misses".

ben: Another angle — could torch.compile be changing the order of ops so KV cache copies move earlier and break cudagraph capture? Maybe the compiled graph inserts an extra copy. Any IR diff?

aisha: I diffed the traced graphs: compile+specialize inserts a small _copy_for_kv op before the first attention call when seq>128; that op has a different buffer aliasing so the capture-compatibility check fails.

kai: So we have three levers: adjust compile specialization to avoid that copy, make capture-compatibility logic looser (tolerate aliasing if buffers are identical after copy), or add autotuner penalty as a short-term fix.

maria: Priorities: short-term autotuner penalty + rollout flag; mid-term tighten compile to avoid unnecessary copies; long-term update capture-compatibility to be more robust.

ben: I'll open a PR for the autotuner score change and add a metric + flag. Suggest default off for dedicated infra while we dry-run on hosted.

aisha: Patch looks good in local canary. I'll run a 24h job across mixed seq distributions and post numbers.

maria: Ping me when you have the dashboard. Also let's note this in the release notes for the optimizer change — call out the torch.compile interaction so teams know to repro if they see regressions.

deploy-bot: canary-deploy: autotuner-penalty-rollout v0.1 deployed to ~5% hosts in us-west. :rocket:

kai: One more thought — add an invariant test: simulate interleaved seq lengths between 1..512 and assert cudagraph_capture_ratio >= 80% or else fail the build for optimizer changes. Could catch regressions early.

aisha: love that. I'll add it to the perf harness.

ben: Filed: GH#4521 autotuner: add capture_compat penalty + metric + rollout flag. Assigning to @ben.

maria: Thanks folks. Good catch. We'll monitor canary and flag if any regressions in p95/p99 pop up. :thumbsup:
